title: A case of atopic dermatitis caused by Ascaris lumbricoides infection
case_text: The patient was a 12-year old female suffering since early infancy from atopic dermatitis and asthma. Both skin and respiratory symptoms were perennial, with worsening in spring and autumn. Allergy testing, performed at the age of 18 months, resulted positive to Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus and farinae. In addition, tomato, hen's egg and cow milk were positive to skin prick tests. Following environmental measures to reduce house dust mite exposure and the elimination of tomato, egg and milk from the diet, there was an improvement of the patient's asthma condition but not in atopic dermatitis. At 3 and 6 years of age, there was a worsening of dermatitis with modest response to topical corticosteroids, while asthma was no longer present. A further worsening of atopic dermatitis occurred at 9 years of age, which was treated with oral bethametasone and topical pimecrolimus. In September 2014, the patient was referred to our Unit; we found peripheral eosinophilia of 14.4% and, suspecting parasitic infections, we evaluated specific IgE for A. lumbricoides, which had a value of 32.50 kU/L. Anthelmintic therapy was prescribed using mebendazole (one 100 mg 1 tablet b.i.d. for 3 days), repeated after 20 and 50 days. Table 1 shows patient data. One month after the first two cycles of therapy, the patient showed progressive improvement of symptoms (Fig. 1), and eosinophilia was 12%. Six months after the end of therapy, the skin was free from dermatitis and a further decrease was observed for eosinophilia (11.20%) and Ascaris-specific IgE (23.90 kU/L).

   - The <case_prompt> represents what an emergency triage clinician knows on Day 1 BEFORE confirmatory tests return.
   - INCLUDE in <case_prompt>: Demographics, travel/occupational/vector exposures (freshwater contact, insect bites, animal exposure), symptom chronology, vital signs, physical exam findings, and initial triage laboratory/imaging results (CBC, platelets, basic metabolic panel, LFTs, urinalysis, plain chest radiograph, bedside ultrasound).
   - STRICTLY EXCLUDE from <case_prompt>:
     * Any mention of the disease name or pathogen genus/species (e.g., do not write "Leptospirosis", "Burkholderia", "Leishmania", "Paragonimus").
     * Confirmatory send-out PCR panels, serological titers, blood culture organism identifications, or biopsy histopathology.
     * The clinical outcome or treatment response (these belong in the diagnostic reasoning, not the presentation).

3. STRUCTURE OF <diagnostic_reasoning>:
   - Enumerate all alternative candidate diagnoses considered in the text.
   - For each candidate, provide a concise summary explaining why it was considered and why it was ruled out in this patient, followed by a direct verbatim quote from the article in quotation marks.
   - Conclude with the Diagnostic Pivot: the pivotal clinical and confirmatory turning point that established the confirmed diagnosis.

4. TARGET CANONICAL DISEASE:
   - The verified ground-truth disease for this patient is: Soil-Transmitted Helminths
   - Disease subtype / specific manifestation: atopic dermatitis caused by Ascaris lumbricoides infection
